**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of a soybean stem at a node
- Gray/dark fuzzy fungal-looking mass concentrated at the node junction
- Surrounding leaves are yellow (late-season senescence)
- No lesions on leaves visible; damage focused on the node area
- Stem otherwise appears green but with dark discoloration at the junction

**Reasoning:**
- The gray-dark growth at the node in a late-season plant (yellowing leaves consistent with R6-R8) matches **Diaporthe** (pod and stem blight), which produces pycnidia/fungal structures at nodes later in the season
- The Diaporthe reference shows dark node lesions with similar gray-brown fungal growth at stem junctions
- Brown_Stem_Rot would show internal pith browning; Anthracnose would show dark acervuli more broadly; Tobacco_Streak_Virus would show streaks and tissue proliferation
- The concentrated node-localized fungal mass in a late-season plant is most consistent with Diaporthe
